strings.species.flora.saltreed.name: Saltreed
strings.species.flora.saltreed.field_note: A reed-like coastal growth with silica threads in its outer leaves. It filters mineral mist and passes the clean water down to its roots. The threads are what the fabricator wants; the plant can spare a few frayed edges.
strings.species.flora.saltreed.hint: Approach a saltreed stand at dusk. Its frayed outer leaves brighten when the mist thickens.
strings.species.flora.glassbell.name: Glassbell
strings.species.flora.glassbell.field_note: A hollow crystal bloom that rings softly when the wind changes. It sequesters salt into its rim and sheds shards as it grows. The bell is an animal shelter as often as it is a mineral deposit.
strings.species.flora.glassbell.hint: Listen for a low chime near the waterline. The clearest bells grow where the tide leaves salt behind.
strings.species.flora.mistmoss.name: Mistmoss
strings.species.flora.mistmoss.field_note: A creeping mat of pale spore filaments. It eats what the tide leaves and holds moisture for the whole understory. sampling it is safe if the colony is brushed, not scraped.
strings.species.flora.mistmoss.hint: Look for a violet sheen on low rocks after the mist lifts.
strings.species.flora.lumen_kelp.name: Lumen kelp
strings.species.flora.lumen_kelp.field_note: A tidal canopy with light-sacs along each frond. The kelp feeds grazers and shelters the reef singer's nurseries. One frond can be cut without killing the plant; the canopy is the point.
strings.species.flora.lumen_kelp.hint: At high tide, the kelp's light-sacs rise close to the surface. Scan from the bank.
strings.species.flora.ash_orchid.name: Ash orchid
strings.species.flora.ash_orchid.field_note: A succession bloom that opens only after ashfall. It trades nectar with the echo moth and stores the rest of its energy underground. The flower is a season, not a decoration.
strings.species.flora.ash_orchid.hint: Find the black soil where cinder rain has settled. The orchid opens for a single dawn.
strings.species.flora.tide_heather.name: Tide heather
strings.species.flora.tide_heather.field_note: A low dune heath that fixes nitrogen for the coast. Its roots hold the bank together. The seed heads comb free in autumn; the roots do not.
strings.species.flora.tide_heather.hint: Look on the dry side of the salt ridge, where the soil is pale and loose.
strings.species.flora.pale_fungus.name: Pale fungus
strings.species.flora.pale_fungus.field_note: A cave decomposer with a faint blue glow. Its mycelium can be older than the landing settlement. The cap is a small harvest; the underground network is not.
strings.species.flora.pale_fungus.hint: Scan the cave mouth at night. The cap light is dim, but it pulses in a slow rhythm.
strings.species.flora.crystal_thistle.name: Crystal thistle
strings.species.flora.crystal_thistle.field_note: A shrub that grows silica spines instead of leaves. It sheds them when the wind shifts. The thistle's living crown is fragile, but the shed spines are abundant.
strings.species.flora.crystal_thistle.hint: Look for a glassy shimmer on the crystal flats. The spines litter the ground beneath the plant.
strings.species.flora.veil_fern.name: Veil fern
strings.species.flora.veil_fern.field_note: A soft understory fern whose fronds condense fog into drinking water. Small animals sleep in the crown. Cut one outer frond and leave the rest.
strings.species.flora.veil_fern.hint: Find the damp hollows beneath the mist line. The fern's pale underside catches the light.
strings.species.flora.silent_bulb.name: Silent bulb
strings.species.flora.silent_bulb.field_note: An ash-season geophyte that stores light in layered scales. The bulb can survive fire; it cannot survive being uprooted. Take one outer scale, if you must.
strings.species.flora.silent_bulb.hint: Scan after dark. The bulb's glow is steady and low, like a lamp under a blanket.
strings.species.flora.drowned_reed.name: Drowned reed
strings.species.flora.drowned_reed.field_note: A brackish filterer with hollow stems. It cleans the marsh and carries its mineral memory back into the water. The reef singers use its roots as a nursery.
strings.species.flora.drowned_reed.hint: Find the standing water behind the tide line. The stems stay green even when submerged.
strings.species.flora.star_cactus.name: Star cactus
strings.species.flora.star_cactus.field_note: A xeric succulent with a radial arm structure. It stores water for years and releases it slowly to the night drifters. The plant can lose one arm and live.
strings.species.flora.star_cactus.hint: On the dry ridge, look for a silhouette with too many arms and not enough leaves.
